liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (1 review, 1 other source): Right channel almost vanishes during Shakedown; reviewer's copy may be normalized or mono for that song; Uploader places this Shakedown Street among the top handful of versions [1][19]
- **Saint Of Circumstance** (1 review): Saint has jaw-dropping Garcia leads and is a standout version, though Sailor>Saint is also liked in the second set [20]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Energetic Truckin' with a nice jam leading into Spoonful [22]
- **Deal** (1 review): Deal's ten minutes feature Garcia shredding almost throughout, from about minute four until the end [26]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Ramble On Rose is tight, with Jerry belting the vocal [26]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer calls Stella Blue phenomenal [27]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Reviewer thinks it is the best Sailor>Saint ever, with high energy and Bobby shouting vocals [28]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 other source): Uploader says Minglewood argues for hiding Bob's slide guitar [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd84-06-30 01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd84-06-30 02 Jack Straw**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd84-06-30 03 Dire Wolf**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd84-06-30 04 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd84-06-30 05 Dupree's Diamond Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd84-06-30 06 Far From Me**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd84-06-30 07 My Brother Esau**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd84-06-30 08 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-06-30.140199.fob.nak700.unknown.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 164 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1984-06-30.senn421.unknown.31225.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 161 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: A tape flip between Rose and Sailor drops a few opening Sailor notes; second-set flip is at the disc two/three split [2]
- **gd1984-06-30.154326.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 166 min [6]
- **gd1984-06-30.162897.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 22 songs; 163 min [7]
- **gd84-06-30.sbd.partial.finney.2542.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 16 songs; 118 min; rated 4.21/5 by 14 [15]. Said about its sound: Sound is superb, but Keep Your Day Job is cut up and the Shakedown has its right channel nearly missing; Reviewer reports great sound quality [19][23]
- **gd84-06-30.aud.set1.cole.18559.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 10 songs; 66 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [17]. Said about its sound: Audience recording of set one only; reviewer says the sound deserves high marks [26]

## Around the show

- The archive copy is a partial first set plus a full second set [20]
- Stage was built at center court of a downtown Indianapolis tennis facility; festival seating on the court, stands on three sides [21]
- Second set was blistering until the drums, then lost steam; a helicopter flew over the stage during the drum solo [21]
- Chairs were folded and piled up, and the crowd danced in dust on soft clay courts [24]
- Attendee says the venue seemed unprepared for a freak-show dance party and ranks it with the Frost or the Greek [24]
- Fans tore up chairs on the clay tennis court and piled them mid-court, startling some locals [25]
- Attendee chatted with a middle-aged man claiming to be a brain surgeon who took a week on tour yearly [25]
- A helicopter with a searchlight flew over the arena, apparently during Space; it doesn't seem audible on the soundboard [27]
- Reviewer offers this show as proof against claims that 1984 was a bad year [19]
- Reviewer calls it a fine example of the intensity of 1984 shows [20]
- Reviewer rates it among the better 1984 shows but says Providence is a truly classic 1984 show [22]
- Reviewer finds it falls short of the Compendium's praise; suggests Merriweather, Cedar Rapids, Berkeley and Ventura as better 1984 samples [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-06-30.140199.fob.nak700.unknown.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Master (FOB) Audience Cassette (11th row, DFC); 3 x Nakamichi CM700 mics > unknown deck > Dat > CDR; Transfer Info: CDR (EAC)> hard disk drive >… [1]
- **gd1984-06-30.senn421.unknown.31225.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Andrew F.; source: FOB, Sennheiser MD-421's > DBX NX-40 > Sony TC-D5 > MAC > unknown > CD [2]. Also: Taper's use of a DBX unit at the show is uncertain; source info is passed on as received [2]
- **gd1984-06-30.154326.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by SBD + AUD Matrix 3 Source Mix (44/16) by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 3 Source Mix (44/16) [6]. Also: This is a matrix mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in November 2021 [6]
- **gd1984-06-30.162897.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Stephen Thomas; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Stephen Thomas' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 capsules > Sony D5M [7]. Also: A Nakamichi 700 source supplies patches: five seconds in the Saint>Deal transition and 21 seconds in Drums [7]
- **gd84-06-30.sbd.partial.finney.2542.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MC>DAT>CDR [15]
- **gd84-06-30.aud.set1.cole.18559.sbeok.shnf**: source: Set 1 FOB MAC (Sennheiser 2 ME-80's & 2 441's 12th row center>sony d-5>WAV>SHN>SHNTOOL>mkwACT. Recorded by Tommy McKeown. sbe fix/seeding by MattMan. [17]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Indianapolis Sports Center - June 30, 1984](https://www.dead.net/show/june-30-1984) [31]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [The Grateful Dead | Saturday, June 30, 1984 …](https://www.flickr.com/photos/194823899@N04/52066221792/) [32]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/194823899@N04/52066221792/) [33]

Energetic Truckin' with a nice jam leading into Spoonful
Reviewer rates it among the better 1984 shows but says Providence is a truly classic 1984 show
Reviewer finds it falls short of the Compendium's praise; suggests Merriweather, Cedar Rapids, Berkeley and Ventura as better 1984 samples
Reviewer reports great sound quality
Chairs were folded and piled up, and the crowd danced in dust on soft clay courts
Attendee says the venue seemed unprepared for a freak-show dance party and ranks it with the Frost or the Greek
Fans tore up chairs on the clay tennis court and piled them mid-court, startling some locals
Attendee chatted with a middle-aged man claiming to be a brain surgeon who took a week on tour yearly
Deal's ten minutes feature Garcia shredding almost throughout, from about minute four until the end
Ramble On Rose is tight, with Jerry belting the vocal
Audience recording of set one only; reviewer says the sound deserves high marks
A helicopter with a searchlight flew over the arena, apparently during Space; it doesn't seem audible on the soundboard
Reviewer calls Stella Blue phenomenal
Reviewer thinks it is the best Sailor>Saint ever, with high energy and Bobby shouting vocals
Uploader says Minglewood argues for hiding Bob's slide guitar
Uploader places this Shakedown Street among the top handful of versions
Uploader calls it a nice capture of one of the better 1984 shows
Taper's use of a DBX unit at the show is uncertain; source info is passed on as received
A tape flip between Rose and Sailor drops a few opening Sailor notes; second-set flip is at the disc two/three split
Early Jack Straw sounds odd from the stage as Healy adjusts and PA volume rises gradually
This is a matrix mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in November 2021
Master cassette source came from Stephen Thomas; Charlie Miller did the transfer and coordinated the effort
A Nakamichi 700 source supplies patches: five seconds in the Saint>Deal transition and 21 seconds in Drums
